evidence: Vulg. Jac. 5.8: quoniam adventus Dominī appropinquāvit
terms.comment: Classically an arrival; the Lord’s coming (adventus Dominī) in the Vulgate, and then the Latin rite’s season of the four Sundays before Christmas. The Byzantine rite has instead the forty-day Nativity Fast (see that record).

phrases.latin: Venī, redēmptor gentium, ostende partum Virginis; mīrētur omne saeculum: tālis decet partus Deum
phrases.english: Come, redeemer of the nations, show the Virgin’s child; let every age marvel: such a birth befits God

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-augustinus), checked against the editions named there.
Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
